strengths: Significance: Reusing historical solutions to accelerate repeated MIP solves is practically useful. PreMIO’s reliance on additional linear constraints makes it accessible through commercial solver interfaces, without modifying solver internals. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b08/review-experiment-o9cvputy/call-794d0de6429f454baad3226ef659bd28/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

Methodological merit: Separate cardinality constraints on predicted zeros and ones provide an interpretable way to tolerate prediction errors. Algorithm 1’s four complementary regions preserve exhaustive coverage, so solving all regions to completion can recover global optimality.

Empirical promise: The evaluation covers three problem families, two commercial solvers, and several internal heuristic settings. Table 1 reports substantial improvements, particularly approximately 3.9–38.4-fold speedups for set covering under the intended interpretation of the metric.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: The framework decomposition and Algorithm 1 make the basic procedure understandable. Remarks 5 and 7 explicitly acknowledge weak theoretical bounds and idealized probability assumptions; these acknowledgments are appropriate. The public and simulated optimization workloads raise no evident material research-ethics concern.
weaknesses: Soundness—central probability argument: Appendix B.1 incorrectly infers unconditional independence of prediction errors from independent training datasets. Errors can remain dependent through the shared test instance; equation (7) invokes additional assumptions about input segments that are neither established nor used experimentally. Furthermore, Theorem 2 applies concentration using unconditional correctness probabilities after selecting U and L through the predictions. A3 does not justify this selection step: with an identically zero optimum and independent rare positive predictions, errors are independent, but every variable selected into U is wrong. The claimed theoretical justification therefore needs substantive repair.

Soundness—connection to implementation: Theorem 3 requires exact conditional solution probabilities and suitable independence of solution variables. Independently fitting classifiers does not establish these properties, and the experiments actually train every classifier on the same dataset. With the experimental setting δ = 0.8, the theorem guarantees only 20% coverage for each individual inequality, providing no useful joint high-confidence guarantee. No calibration, optimum-retention, or parameter-sensitivity measurements validate the practical interpretation. Training some SCP models with a 10% optimality gap further separates the labels from the optimal solutions assumed in the analysis.

Evaluation and significance: Section 4 solves only the favored restricted subproblem for 120 seconds, then measures how long the original solver takes to reach PreMIO’s own best objective. This can demonstrate useful time-to-target behavior, but it does not establish faster globally certified optimization or sufficiently good solution quality. The paper supplies no objective gaps, absolute runtimes, or evaluation of the complete four-region algorithm. Handling of infeasible restricted problems and targets not reached within the baseline’s 3600-second limit is unspecified.

Originality and attribution: Section 1.1 already identifies prediction-distance constraints in Ding et al. [11] and existing multivariable branching methods. The interpretable cardinality construction is a potentially useful refinement, but comparisons only against unaugmented solvers do not establish its added value over learned local branching, variable fixing, warm starts, or neural diving. Ablations are also needed to distinguish benefits from the concentration-based thresholds from benefits of simply restricting the search.

Reproducibility—instance generation: The MKP generator divides each row sum by 4n when constructing capacities. With coefficients uniform on 1–1000, this gives capacities around 125 across 10 or 30 constraints, making individually feasible items extremely unlikely and typically leaving only the all-zero solution. This appears inconsistent with the reported challenging MKP experiments and requires clarification or correction. The SCP configuration (1000, 20000) in the setup also becomes (2000, 10000) in Table 1.

Reproducibility and statistical support: Although several experimental details are provided, there is no accompanying code or instance release identified, and Gurobi/COPT versions, thread counts, random seeds, and logistic-regression fitting settings are missing. Only five SCUC test instances are used per configuration, with no uncertainty estimates or repeated-run analysis. Aggregate ratios alone cannot establish the stability of the reported gains.

Presentation accuracy: Section 4.1 defines speedup as mean T_PreMIO divided by mean T_Original, while the figures and discussion interpret values above one as improvements—the reciprocal convention. This must be corrected and checked against the underlying measurements. Such inconsistencies materially impede assessment of otherwise promising results.
